translation: The target consists of three definitions of object-language formulas (with no theorem or provability claim asserted): (1) Def15 is a function taking two natural numbers a and b and returning the atomic formula atom 0 a b (with first index 0 and variable arguments a and b in that order). (2) Def16 is a constant of type Form defined as all 0 (iff (K (neg (Def15 0 0))) (Def15 1 0)), i.e., the formula obtained by applying the universal quantifier all for variable 0 to the object-language biconditional (iff, defined via and, neg, imp, and fls) whose left-hand side is K applied to the negation (neg) of atom 0 0 0 and whose right-hand side is atom 0 1 0; variable 0 is bound by all 0, while variable 1 is unbound (occurs free). (3) Def17 is a constant of type Form defined as neg (Def15 1 1), i.e., the object-language negation (imp (atom 0 1 1) fls) of atom 0 1 1, in which variable 1 occurs free.
